resolved_problems.canonical_en: The treatment outcome for this hospitalization is recorded as improved; however, this does not mean that all active problems have been resolved

treatment_readiness.canonical_en: The intravenous chemotherapy treatment phase recorded for the current record has been completed and was documented as improved; however, because of electrolyte abnormalities, leukopenia, and persistent/indeterminate tumor imaging findings, entry into the next treatment cycle requires repeat laboratory results and oncology assessment.

hard_failure_rules_en: Interpret partial imaging improvement as complete remission, cure, or no residual lesion

Directly terminate continuity management without arranging oncology follow-up and re-examination.

stopping.rationale_en: The current evidence records improvement after the hospitalization and provides no evidence of a terminal state. Oncology treatment and monitoring should not be stopped because persistent or indeterminate imaging abnormalities and leukopenia, electrolyte disturbances, anemia, and nutritional/inflammatory abnormalities remain.
remaining_blockers_en: It is still necessary to confirm that electrolyte and hematologic abnormalities have been corrected, are stable, or have a clear outpatient management plan.
A subsequent chemotherapy/oncologic treatment plan still needs to be formulated
Planned follow-up is still needed for residual and indeterminate imaging abnormalities

question.question_en: At this time point, use only available evidence to identify key evidence, supported claims, patient state, appropriate next actions, and whether stopping or follow-up is safe.
